The test image shows corn plants with orange-brown to rusty-colored streaks/discoloration running along the leaves. This points strongly to leaf diseases. Top candidates: Common_Rust, Southern_Rust, Stewart_S_Disease, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Goss_S_Wilt.

Let me view reference images one at a time across classes.

Now let me make my assessment. I've viewed 16+ reference images across all major leaf disease classes. 

Reviewing the test image: corn plants viewed from below looking up, showing **widespread orange-brown to rusty coloration on the stalks/leaf sheaths and some leaves**. The coloration is orange-cinnamon colored and covers large areas.

Key comparisons:
- **Southern_Rust** (Corn_Disease_120.jpg): dense orange-cinnamon pustules covering leaf surface with yellowing — closest visual match. Southern Rust also characteristically spreads to leaf sheaths and stalks.
- **Physoderma_Brown_Spot** (Corn_Disease_3.jpg): orange-rusty spots on leaf blades with dark spots on midrib — partially similar but coloration is more yellowish-brown.
- **Common_Rust**: darker reddish-brown discrete pustules — does not match the lighter orange tone.
- All other classes (NLB, GLS, Stewart's, Goss's Wilt, Eyespot, Tar Spot, etc.) showed clearly different symptom patterns.

The widespread orange-rusty appearance of the test image, with coloring visible on leaf sheaths and multiple plant surfaces, best matches Southern_Rust, which is known to spread to stalks and leaf sheaths and shows cinnamon-orange pustules.
